sections.title: Habit and range
sections.text: Corylus colurna, Turkish hazel, is a single-trunk deciduous tree native from south-eastern Europe to Iran. It can reach about 12–15 m. Its leaves are toothed and its hazelnuts are enclosed in a deeply divided involucre.

sections.title: Fruit and comparison
sections.text: The hazelnuts are edible. The plate matches the single-trunk tree and the fringed fruit husks. Corylus avellana more often forms a multi-stemmed shrub; both produce hazelnuts, but their habit and husks differ.
